title: Interlinked Macroporous 3D Scaffolds from Microgel Rods
protocol: Use 1 mL and 5 mL glass syringes and syringe pumps for the microfluidic procedure.
Design the microfluidic chip using computer-aided design software.
Produce a master template as previously reported.
Achieve controlled UV-irradiation using a self-constructed UV-LED (λ = 365 nm).
Ensure sufficient cooling by external airflow if local heat generation occurs during irradiation.
Prepare 20 g of a 10:1 mass mixture of polydimethylsiloxane and curing agent.
Mix the PDMS and curing agent vigorously for 3 min.
Mix 60 mg of Oil Red O in 2.0 g of toluene.
Add 50 μL of Oil Red O in toluene solution to the PDMS mixture.
Mix until there is homogeneous color distribution.
Remove bubbles by placing the mixture into a desiccator with a vacuum pump.
Cast the PDMS mixture into the master template to a height of 5-5.5 mm.
Degas again after casting.
Allow the PDMS to cure for 18 h at room temperature.
Cut out the PDMS structure.
Punch inlet and outlet holes into the PDMS structure using a line core sampling tool.
Wash the PDMS with isopropanol and deionized water repeatedly five times.
Remove liquid from the PDMS via pressured air or nitrogen flow after each washing step.
Treat dry glass and PDMS together in a plasma oven at 0.2 mbar, oxygen flow of 20 mL/min for 60 s at 100 W.
Connect the glass and PDMS directly to form the microfluidic device.
Avoid bending the PDMS structure during binding to minimize channel deformation.
Place the device with 50 µL of trichloro-(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluoroctyl)-silane in a desiccator under vacuum overnight.
Rinse the outside of the device with hydrofluoroether.
Weigh out 33.3 mg of star-polyethylene glycol-acrylate (sPEG-AC) and 3.03 mg of lithium phenyl-2,4,6-trimethylbenzoylphosphinate (LAP).
Dissolve 18.74 mg of 2-aminoethyl methacrylate hydrochloride (AMA) in 1.5 ml of deionized water and pass through a syringe filter with a 0.20 μm pore size.
Use sterile 36 mM GRGDS-PC aliquots prepared in water and stored at -20°C.
Dissolve sPEG-AC and LAP using 291.7 μl of the AMA solution, then add 8.3 μl of the GRGDS-PC solution.
Protect the amine component prepolymer solution from light using aluminum foil.
Weigh 33.3 mg of star-polyethylene glycol-acrylate (sPEG-AC) and 3.03 mg of LAP for epoxy component prepolymer solution.
Dissolve sPEG-AC and LAP in 300 μl of deionized water, then add 2.4 mg of glycidyl methacrylate (GMA).
Protect the epoxy component prepolymer solution from light using aluminum foil.
Insert the needles into the PE tubes and remove the gas from the syringe and the tube.
Insert a PE tube into the outlet for product collection.
Place all the glass syringes in the syringe pumps and insert each tubing end into the corresponding inlet.
Protect the prepolymer tubing from light via aluminum foil or a black tube to avoid unintentional gelation.
Focus the microscope on the oil-water cross-section.
Start the first oil syringe pump (flow rate = 100-200 µL/h) to fill the channel with oil first to prevent channel wetting by the disperse phase.
Decrease the first oil flow rate to 30 µL/h.
Start the prepolymer syringe pump at a flow rate between 100-200 µL/h until the dispersed aqueous phase is observed at the cross-section.
Set the prepolymer flow rate to 30 µL/h and focus the microscope on the outlet.
Start the second oil syringe pump with a flow rate of 300 µL/h and wait for the flow regime to stabilize.
Place the outlet tube in a collection container, positioning it in the upper part of the container to avoid pressure increase due to product accumulation over time.
Set the UV irradiation system such that the irradiance is between 900-1000 mW/cm² with an irradiation spot in the straight channel part before the outlet.
Adjust the flow rates of the prepolymer and first oil to achieve a desired aspect ratio within the range of 3.0 to 4.5.
Set the irradiation time for the dispersed phase to approximately 2.3 seconds, depending on the size of the irradiation spot.
Start UV irradiation and adjust the flow rates if necessary according to previous adjustments.
Observe the production at the beginning and monitor for stable flow behavior in the outlet and the uniformity of the microgel rods.
Adjust the second oil flow to optimize product transport within the outlet.
Change the collection container and note the product collection start time and flow rates.
Protect the product from dust.
Stop collecting before any syringe runs low on solution.
Remove the collection container and note the time when stopping collection.
Stop irradiation and all the syringe pumps.
Wash the product subsequently 5 times each with n-hexane, isopropanol, and deionized water.
Disperse the product carefully after each solution addition and wait 10 min before replacing the solvent.
Replace the isopropanol gradually with water to prevent the rods from floating to the surface of the liquid.
Perform multiple additional washing steps with water to decrease remaining isopropanol traces.
Determine the number of microgel rods per dispersion volume for the epoxy and amine functionalized samples.
Adjust the number of epoxy and amine functionalized samples by dilution or concentration to a similar value between 1,000-5,000 rods/100 µL.
Centrifuge the mixture at ~2,000 x g for 5-10 s to speed up sedimentation.
Transfer the first component dispersion into a conical 1.5 mL or 2 mL transparent vial.
Add the second component in a controlled manner using a pipette (100 μL).
Mix the contents directly with the pipette after addition.
Calculate the theoretical number of epoxy groups in the interlinked structure based on flow rate, number of microgels collected, and dilution factor.
Add GRGDS-PC solution to the interlinked structure to modify all remaining epoxy groups with the cell adhesive peptide bearing a free amine and thiol (n[theoretical epoxy groups]/n[GRGDS-PC] = 1).
Leave at room temperature overnight.
Wash with deionized water to remove unreacted molecules.
Remove the supernatant from the scaffold.
Reduce the water level in the vial to just submerge the interlinked scaffold.
Irradiate with UV light of λ = 250-300 nm.
Close the vial and transfer it onto a clean bench.
Wash once with sterile water.
Replace the water in the vial with cell culture media and allow for equilibration for 5 min.
Repeat washing with fresh cell culture media twice.
Transfer the macroporous scaffold into a cell culture well plate by pouring or using a spatula.
